scope: Optional caller-supplied synchronous KMS SDK bridge. Protocol-double and existing CF1/keyring tests only.

official_sources.title: Encryption context - AWS Key Management Service

findings: Both boto3 operations accept KeyId, EncryptionContext and EncryptionAlgorithm. The adapter sends the exact deployment key ARN and SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT on every request.

Encrypt returns binary CiphertextBlob, key ARN and algorithm. Decrypt returns binary Plaintext, key ARN and algorithm. The adapter requires the exact pinned response identity and algorithm, with a 32-byte plaintext root.
KMS symmetric encryption context is authenticated and requires an exact case-sensitive match on decrypt. It is public metadata and may appear in CloudTrail.

The host supplies SDK installation, credentials, endpoint, timeout and bounded retry configuration. The adapter performs no discovery, retry, remote key administration or key-generation policy change.
Async unwrap moves the blocking SDK call to a thread. Cancellation rejects late material but cannot cancel already dispatched remote work. Inherited provider objects refuse use after fork.

verification.database_ddl: eight existing CF1 PostgreSQL persistence cases; new protocol tests have no database DDL

limits: No boto3/botocore installation or actual SDK transport was exercised.
No live AWS account, workload identity, IAM policy, endpoint, network retries/timeouts, native audit log, concurrency limit, key disable/deletion or external custody was exercised.
No production provider is designated. All seven production qualification gates remain UNKNOWN.
Wrappers remain opaque provider bytes within the existing WrappedRoot contract; CF1 frames and KeyPolicy semantics are unchanged.
Python immutable bytes provide no verified zeroization guarantee. Caller-supplied SDK objects remain a trusted host boundary.
